statements.text: Limiting the current existing dual prices policy in Chile for raw materials. Currently, Chile reserves 25% of the production for locally established companies at preferential prices.

There are products exempted from the application of this additional tariff, such as refined copper and wood, which continue to be exempt from tariffs on their import into the U.S., in accordance with the FTA.

The trade agreement would also help cushion the negative effects of the US Inflation Reduction Act (IRA), which provides subsidies for renewable energies and electric vehicles from local players or countries that have a free trade agreement with the US – like Chile

April 2, 2025: “Liberation Day”: The U.S. President announces the General Additional Tariff of 10% on most imports from the majority of countries (including Chile) not included in a Specific Tariff list
July 30, 2025: announcement of 50% tariff imposed on semi-finished copper products, effective August 1.

On July 30, 2025, the United States imposed an additional 50% tariff on the value of the copper content of semi-finished or derived products with high copper content (e.g., tubes, wires, rods, sheets, electric cables, and copper-based accessories), effective from August 1, 2025.

Exports from Chile to the U.S. will continue to be subject to the General Additional Tariff of 10%, which is applied over the 0% tariff established in the Free Trade Agreement (FTA) between both countries.
